misconceptions.description: Treating how many teachers recommend a tool as proof it is effective or safe
misconceptions.trigger: candidate adopts a resource because it is popular or admired, skipping the evidence and data check
misconceptions.feedback: Treat the network as a source to vet. Check the evidence, the recommenders' relevance, and the tool's data handling.

misconceptions.description: Adopting a colleague's strategy without checking whether their context matches the placement
misconceptions.trigger: candidate borrows a strategy from a different school context without naming the gap
misconceptions.feedback: Name the context gap between the source and your placement, then test whether the strategy survives your constraints.

misconceptions.description: Sharing AI-provided citations into a network without verifying they exist
misconceptions.trigger: candidate passes on study citations she could not locate
misconceptions.feedback: Unverifiable citations are a fabrication signal. Rely only on sources you can locate and check before sharing them.

misconceptions.description: Treating likes, follows, or reshares as a professional contribution to the network
misconceptions.trigger: candidate reports engagement metrics instead of tested evidence and context cautions
misconceptions.feedback: Contribute by reporting what you tried, where it worked and did not, and the caution colleagues need to judge fit.
